Does anyone else have an issue with the concept of "healthcare as a right for all"?

Rights like free speech, gun ownership, due process, etc are conveyed to us without putting a burden on another party. Healthcare as a right says I have a claim on the labor of a healthcare worker. This seems wrong.

If they wanted to do something, they should have just passed single payer when they controlled congress and the white house. Instead, they were too busy trying to protect their corporate constituents and their own jobs. I get that it was politically unpopular, but what we ended up with is pretty much a cluster fuck.

Due process requires quite a bit of labor from everyone employed by the justice system. Being guaranteed due process implies that we'll have to hire police officers, judges, and lawyers to provide those services. The right to healthcare is no different. In both cases, you will be paid for your services. Also in both cases, you're free to choose a career outside of this field if you want. If you don't like the idea of having to hear every case that comes before you, then don't be a judge. If you don't like the idea of having to heal every patient you see, don't be a doctor.

The argument just doesn't hold water.

In any society based on law, with or without due process, we have to have law officers and judges. Lawyers may be optional without due process, but they're optional in our system as well in that I don't have to hire one if I'm accused of a crime, the state will provide one free of charge.

In this system, if I'm sick, the state isn't providing medical care, I still have to pay for it. That isn't a "right" when the cost and quality of care is still radically different based on income.
